answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure on SMB creates urgency, but memory_73 clearly warns that promotional pricing materially harms 30-day retention—exactly the opposite of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The competitor's move exploits price sensitivity, but matching it would replicate a known retention damage pattern. Instead, deploy a dual strategy grounded in confirmed wins: (1) Activation messaging (memory_91: +11% engagement, +6% activation, +1% retention lift) to deepen engagement and perceived value among at-risk SMB accounts, reducing churn sensitivity to price; (2) Referral incentives (memory_57: strong revenue, no retention harm) to convert remaining price-sensitive SMB into advocates, offsetting some churn with qualified inbound. This preserves the enterprise sales-assist channel for high-value prospects (memory_44) without diluting it. A standard_experiment scale lets us measure SMB-specific retention impact before broader rollout. This avoids the retention cliff of promotional pricing while leveraging psychological engagement and organic growth—more defensible long-term than discounting.
